page: Amazon Web Services c4.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the Xen hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor running at 2.9 GHz. The configuration includes 8 vCPUs, which correspond to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, and 15.0 GB of system memory, yielding 1.88 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the c4.2xlarge in the average performance tier for most CPU and memory operations. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yield scores of 1470.98 and 7763.44 respectively, while the Geekbench multi-core score reaches 4493.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 423.32 GB/sec and an uncached large block write speed of 37.86 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (28.83 GB/sec) and Redis SET operations (3.14 million operations/sec) register as weak relative to other instances. Large-model LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with the medium 7B model achieving a poor prompt processing speed of 11.57 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4.2xlarge offers a balanced allocation of dedicated compute resources without the added expense of bundled local storage. This makes it suitable for compute-bound workloads that rely on network-attached storage. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, software compilation, image processing, and moderate CPU-based physics simulations. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale Redis deployments, or modern large language model inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c4.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server featuring 8 vCPUs and 15.0 GB of memory, running on an Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor at 2.9 GHz. Utilizing the Xen hypervisor and x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates dedicated CPU resources but does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. It offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Performance benchmarks generally fall into the average tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 4493.0 and a static web serving throughput of 6.85 GB/sec. However, it exhibits weaker performance in multi-threaded decompression and Redis operations, and poor throughput for medium-sized LLM inference. Qualitatively, the c4.2xlarge provides a cost-effective option for compute-heavy tasks that do not require local NVMe storage. It is best suited for workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, image processing, and moderate CPU-based simulations.
